title: 2023 property tax ratios and 2022 financial results
subtitle: Municipal accommodation tax policy, Integrity Commissioner reappointment, airport fees, reserves, and short-term rental tax questions
overview: The Administration and Finance Committee recommended keeping the 2023 property class tax ratios unchanged, including 1.9500 for multi-residential, commercial and industrial properties {{vote:m4}}. It also asked staff to report back later in 2023 on options for the multi-residential ratio in 2024 and beyond. Staff noted that the province is reviewing multi-residential taxation. Council will consider the tax rate by-laws on April 19, 2023, which is one of the last steps before local municipalities issue final tax bills.

The committee recommended approving a Municipal Accommodation Tax Investment Policy {{vote:m5}}. The policy sets out how to allocate money that has built up in a reserve from the cost-sharing arrangement between the Region and area municipalities. It also recommended approving the 2022 year-end results and applying the Surplus Allocation Policy {{vote:m6}}. The Region ended 2022 with a consolidated surplus of $7.2 million.

On the consent agenda the committee recommended reappointing Aird & Berlis LLP as Integrity Commissioner for 2023 to 2027 and amending the fees and charges by-law for Waterloo International Airport. Other items were received for information.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended keeping the 2023 property class tax ratios unchanged, directing staff to prepare the related by-laws for April 19 and to report back on multi-residential ratio options for 2024 and beyond.
The committee recommended approving a policy for allocating money accumulated in the accommodation tax reserve.
The committee recommended receiving the 2022 Plan Update, approving the preliminary 2022 financial results for the audited statements, and applying the Surplus Allocation Policy.
The committee recommended reappointing Aird & Berlis LLP as Integrity Commissioner for a four-year term from June 1, 2023 to May 31, 2027.
The committee recommended amending the fees and charges by-law to include new and adjusted Waterloo International Airport fees.

debate: On tax ratios, one councillor asked whether affordable units could be taxed differently from full-market multi-residential units. Staff said legislation does not allow this through the tax ratio process, though other approaches exist and could be examined in the upcoming review.
Staff said the province is reviewing property taxation and appears intended to lower multi-residential ratios, which was part of the case for reviewing the Region's ratio.

On wastewater, staff attributed the 2022 variance to a dry summer, which reduced flow to treatment plants, and to sharply higher chemical costs, especially chlorine. Staff said 2023 budgeting accounted for both.

Councillors questioned the tax stabilization reserve. Staff said about $8 million is planned for the 2023 operating budget, and that other reserves could be considered in an emergency, though many are committed to future capital needs. One councillor asked for a reserve policy review timeline at the next meeting.

Councillors asked about the lobbyist registry timeline, with a summer 2023 staff update to be added to the tracking list. One also raised short-term rentals missing from the accommodation tax, and staff said they would look into it.
